description_full: easyJet plc operates as a low-cost airline carrier in Europe. The company engages in the development of building projects; financing and insurance business; and tour operator activities, as well as provides holiday packages. It also offers heavy base maintenance and air transport services. easyJet plc was founded in 1995 and is headquartered in Luton, the United Kingdom.
ceo_bio: Mr. Alistair Kenton Jarvis | CEO, Member of the Management Board & Director | Age 57 | Compensation: $2.4M (FY2025)
financial_summary: easyJet Plc is a mid-cap industrials business with a $6.7B market cap on $13.2B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 17% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $817M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 4.5×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 7% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.62x).
It accounts for 0.3% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 550 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 39% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 3% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 43% and a beta of 1.05, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.51 vs 5y 1.07), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $42K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 70% in the 2020 crash and 69% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 42% below its DCF fair value of $15.53, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 17%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $7.13 to $37.22 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Industrials peers: cheaper on P/E 12.3 vs 23.1 and P/FCF 8.2 vs 22.4, richer on EV/EBITDA 18.9 vs 13.3 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 12.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 14.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The Street target $6.12 on average, 32% below the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 20.0% annual cash-flow growth, 15pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 14% earns above the cost of capital of 7.6%, but the 7pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.75).
It runs a 17% gross margin and converts 6% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 9/9 and cash conversion of 3.29x.
ROE of 14% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (3.3x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $788.6M.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.64 in the distress zone.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 21.4% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 14.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 0%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.1% (2.0% in dividends, less 0.9% of net share issuance).
